unsure: The fix uses argPt (erasedValueClassArg of the class type) rather than the reviewer's result.tpe.widen. widen fixes only the constant cases: the base also crashes, with no constant involved, for an argument narrower than the underlying type (R(s: String) vs R(o: AnyRef), St(null) vs a value of type St, G[AnyRef]("s") vs g: G[AnyRef]) and for a literal-type value class (class Lit(val x: 7)), where widening would newly break agreement with values typed ErasedValueType(Lit, Int(7)). argPt makes every injection's type equal to the erasure of the class type. Consequence: after posterasure the argument tree carries the underlying type instead of its own narrower type (e.g. Nothing for a throw, String for an AnyRef-underlying class). I found no consumer relying on the narrower type (bytecode identical for stdlib, existing value-class tests and the edge cases above), but a reviewer should consider posterasure's AsInstanceOf elimination (v.tpe <:< tpe), which could keep a cast it used to drop when the argument's own type was narrower than the underlying; I saw no instance. A value class over another value class is not allowed, so that variant is not tested. The JUnit test pins bytecode shapes (assertSameSummary) that the backend could change independently.
note: Type the InjectDerivedValue tree with ErasedValueType(cls, erasedValueClassArg(tref)) instead of the argument's type, so injections agree with each other and with other values of the class and the lub taken when erasure retypes a conditional receiver succeeds. Regression in 2.11.0 from scala/scala#3082.
